<!-- pr-reviewer: 65deeffd740e6a7f41e19336e2c5989d054c5a1a -->
**Needs changes before merge** - one process item (the breaking-change marker); the code and the safety floor check out.

## What looks good
- Migration (`project/fidelity_migrate.rs`, wired at `project/apply.rs:513`): a pre-v59 file marks every model with facets and every from-model stock copy that has no recorded `coarse_mm`; a #911-era recorded chord is kept; the mark is saved as `fidelity_unknown` (never as a chord number) so a re-save cannot turn it into "fine". A v59 file is not migrated again, and the version check still refuses anything newer than v59. No id or existing field moves for a current project (project_roundtrip, float_roundtrip green; `fidelity_unknown` is skipped when false).
- Every reader treats the sentinel as refused, never as full fidelity: `op_problem` (`model_fidelity.rs`, names the model and says re-import), `verdict_tol` / `program_tol` (so the sim and the eye judge nothing), `gate_problems` (an unknown fixture gets its own line), `fixture::steel_box` (plain box, since the gate refuses the post anyway). `op_coarse` takes the max chord, so the sentinel always wins over a known one. UI model page, MCP `get_job` and script API use `summary` / `facts` and say "Fidelity unknown", never the number.
- Re-import clears it through `UpdateModel`, a command, and its undo restores the mark (pinned). A row with both `fidelity_unknown` and `coarse_mm`, or the mark on a non-mesh entity, is refused before any world write (`project/validate.rs`).
- No new unwrap/expect/panic outside tests; new module has a provenance line and is well under 400 lines; no new user-facing command, so no MCP tool owed (#1339 is named in the decision file for the "vouch" command); no process files changed, so no PROCESS_VERSION bump needed; no snapshot PNGs touched; examples re-stamped v59 only by version number.

## Local results (PR head trial-merged with upstream/main, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | app suites ok (196 s; incl. fidelity_copies, coarse_laws, model_fidelity, step_budget, project_roundtrip, float_roundtrip, mcp, microarc_test_part, fixtures/setup suites), ui suites ok (29 s) |
| `golden_cl` | 26 passed |
| ui lib, `--test-threads=1`, filters model_fidelity / step_budget / tool_body | 21 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Mutation check: making `model_fidelity::is_unknown` always return false (unknown reads as a known chord) turns `fidelity_copies::a_project_saved_before_fidelity_was_recorded_loads_unknown_and_refuses_until_reimported` red (panic at `fidelity_copies.rs:276`); reverted afterwards.

## Requested before merge
1. Mark the break. AGENTS.md "Commits and Releases": an incompatible project-file or post-output change says so with `!` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. This bumps the project format to v59 and makes every pre-v59 project refuse its operations until re-import, and the PR body itself calls it breaking, yet the title is `fix(project):` and neither commit nor the body has a `BREAKING CHANGE:` line (the body has a "## Breaking" heading only). Make it `fix(project)!:` (or add a `BREAKING CHANGE:` line to the body, which needs no push) so the cut computes the right bump and release notes lead with it.

## Notes (not blocking)
- Only one pre-v59 fixture pin (the v58 file made in the test, plus `step_block_371` v56 in the ui lib); it covers load, refusal, re-save, re-import/undo and the corrupt row, which is enough, but a checked-in v58 file with a coarse-recorded model would guard the "recorded chord is kept" branch against a future refactor.
- Not exercised by the review: the GUI by hand, and the release-lane gpu_render docs test.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
